Senate passes budget bill after late-night session

By Staff

WASHINGTON — The Senate passed the budget bill 52–48 early Thursday after a late-night session that stretched past 2 a.m., sending the measure to the House where its fate is uncertain.

The bill, which funds the government through September, includes a modest increase in defense spending and a freeze on most domestic programs, according to the summary released by the committee.

Opponents said the measure was rushed. "We have not had time to read it," one senator said on the floor, while supporters argued that a shutdown would be far worse for the country than an imperfect bill.

The House is expected to take up the bill next week. Leadership has not said whether it has the votes, and several members have signaled they will oppose it unless changes are made.
